fixture: OTA output-swing / gain-compression bench (issue #331): design/ota/ota_fd.spice as committed on main, one instance per load, in the closed-loop integrate-phase configuration the integrator presents (driven Cs + parked Cs + Cp on the summing node, Ci feedback, beta = Ci/(Ci+2Cs+Cp), 1.1 pF external load per side), swept over the DR-002 anchor set
result_kind: simulated (ngspice, transistor-level netlist of design/ota/ota_fd; not the behavioural model). A simulated number is never called measured.
evidence_source: T (step 1 of the operator ruling on #148, 2026-11-17)

a.label: main
a.source: design/integrator as on main: Ci = Cs/0.5 = 2 pF (C1 = C2 = 0.5)

b.label: c0p3
b.source: PR #257 rescale (DR-007): Ci = Cs/0.3 = 3.334 pF drawn (40.64 x 40.64 um cap_mim_m3_1), design/integrator/SIZING.md at PR #257 head 80167c7d1f8cf7e195cf66ed5652207528e0a6d1

corner_set.name: DR-002 anchor set
corner_set.subset_statement: DR-002 anchor set (7 points), a declared subset of the full 45-point grid, as DR-002 allows for expensive sweeps

method.sequence: per amplitude (0.2 Vpp small-signal reference, then 0.4-2.8 Vpp) and polarity: 250 ns reset (ideal switches short out<->summing node, unity feedback, vod -> 0), 5 accumulated plate steps of one clock's charge transfer each (120 ns apart, the phase is 97.66 ns), then a hold past the phase; the step edges are bench drives on ideal capacitor plates, not switch edges, and the driven-plate excursion is Ci/Cs x the output swing by charge conservation -- bench-only, on linear capacitors, and it does not touch the settled operating point the gain is extracted from
method.extraction: A_eff = |vod| / (beta * (|target| - |vod|)), the inversion of the finite-gain error 1/(beta*A) of the settled closed-loop charge transfer; beta is computed from the bench capacitor values (Cp = 35 fF per side, the hand-calc value the settling benches also keep; the OTA's own input capacitance is not in it, which is why the 0.2 Vpp reference point is gated against the ota-gain record rather than assumed exact)
method.compression_points: first amplitude where the extracted gain has fallen 1 dB / 3 dB below its small-signal value (the 0.2 Vpp reference point), linearly interpolated on the gain-vs-swing curve; the worse of the two polarities
method.settledness_gate: every segment is read twice, 150 ns apart, and the record refuses if the output moved more than 5 mV
method.leaves_out: slew and settling dynamics inside the phase (sim/ota-settling owns those), noise, mismatch (nominal grid), layout parasitics, and the switch-charge-injection effects sim/integrator-ci owns

no_spec_budget: there is no ratified swing row this record grades against: spec 5.4's ~1.39 Vpp figure is the number the #148 ruling wants clarified, and this record is the simulated evidence that clarification waits on. `pass` below is the validity verdict (all anchors measured, all segments settled, the small-signal reference matching sim/ota-gain), not a spec verdict.

swing_reference.note: The integrator swings this bench interpolates its gain at. Not merged: PR #257 is on an operator ratification hold, and this bench does not depend on it merging -- the c0p3 cell values are parameterised from that PR's design/integrator/SIZING.md, and the swing points are read from its c0p3 modulator record. If that PR re-records before merging, re-derive C0P3_SWINGS in run_swing.py from the merged record and re-run this bench.

comparison_column.why: its open-loop ac gain at vod = 0 is the small-signal value this bench's 0.2 Vpp reference must reproduce; the gate tolerance is 0.5 dB (the reference is a secant over 0.2 Vpp, not the vod = 0 tangent, and beta omits the OTA's input capacitance)
